abstract: Protein protein interactions underlie many extracellular defense and protease regulatory processes, yet identifying their structural interfaces directly in complex biological samples remains challenging. Limited proteolysis coupled with mass spectrometry provides peptide level readouts of local protease accessibility, but linking condition dependent peptide recovery to structural regions in endogenous proteomes requires complementary analysis. Here, we report peptide level assay of protein interaction (PLAPI) using combinatorial native and denatured proteolysis. A single human serum specimen was analyzed in three paired technical preparations using brief trypsin digestion under native conditions and extended digestion after denaturation, followed by isotopic diethyl labeling and LCMS/MS. Applying a 2 of 3 detection rule yielded 920 denatured only peptides and 124 peptides detected under both conditions, with no native only peptides. Mapping to the reference structures placed 13 denatured only C3b peptides at the Factor B binding interface and identified multiple denatured only A2M intersubunit contact regions. Within the A2M bait region, adjacent peptides exhibited different detection patterns; two were detected under both conditions, whereas one was detected only after denaturation. STRING association and enrichment analyses linked the candidate proteins to extracellular defense and protease regulation. These results indicate that PLAPI can provide peptide level evidence for prioritizing structural regions in complex serum samples and guide focused follow up analyses.
